title: Very ampleness from separating closed points and nonzero tangent vectors by sections
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: Over an algebraically closed field, for a proper k-scheme X, an invertible sheaf L and a subspace V of H^0(X, L) that separates distinct closed points and separates nonzero tangent vectors from the vanishing locus, the lemma concludes that L is very ample and the canonical morphism to P(V) is a closed immersion (statement lines 4308-4324). The proof first notes that (1) makes V generate L, so the canonical morphism exists, and that it is proper; injectivity on closed points together with properness makes the morphism finite. The remaining and substantive step is surjectivity of O_{P(V)} to phi_*O_X, checked on stalks at closed points: condition (1) makes the fibre over p a singleton, so the stalk map is a finite module map between local rings, the residue fields are both k by the Nullstellensatz, and condition (2) makes the map on tangent spaces injective, i.e. the map on cotangent spaces surjective, which by the standard local criterion forces the stalk map to be surjective (proof lines 4326-4383). The claim is H2: the reduction to finiteness is quick, and the final local algebra step is the part that carries the content.
